conceptZh: 包：勹包住巳，把東西包起來。
object: a stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker with an oversized magnifying glass, and a pale steamed bun
morph: the pig proudly builds a silly wrong shape, spots it through the magnifying glass, shrugs and fixes it into 包
creativeAngle: 豬探長先拼出怪怪的形狀，放大鏡一照發現錯了，一秒修好成包。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 包 (bun / bag), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker with an oversized magnifying glass, and a pale steamed bun. Light beige backdrop with a faint desk edge; the glyph is deep burgundy. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: a stout pig detective in a checked hat waddles in, hauling a magnifying glass bigger than himself; the voice says the first 包 as he flips open a mystery bundle and burgundy strokes tumble out. 1.5-3.0s: he proudly arranges them into a wobbly blob with a dot in the wrong spot and tips his hat. The voice says the second 包 as the magnifying glass swings up, his eye grows huge, and he spots the mistake. 3.0-4.5s: he shrugs, taps one stroke, and the whole shape slides into the proper 包 at 70% of frame height. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 書包 (ㄕㄨ ㄅㄠ) as a little backpack plops beside him, its flap pops open, and he peeks in. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is still; the pig tips his hat as the magnifying glass sways at the edge. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Voice: one gentle off-screen voice in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, slow with crisp tones, reads precisely 包、包、書包 = ㄅㄠ、ㄅㄠ、ㄕㄨ ㄅㄠ, character, character, word, and nothing after it. Keep any background music quieter than the voice. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 包 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.

conceptZh: 浣熊助手花生踮著腳把包子一顆顆疊成搖搖欲墜的高塔，積木小隊還爬上去加高，他在最糟的時刻放手敬禮，整座塔轟然倒下，積木摔成勹、包子擠成巳，剛好堆出「包」，花生被埋在包子堆裡只剩眼睛。
object: a wobbling tower of pale steamed buns topped by a squad of interlocking building bricks, stacked by a cartoon raccoon sidekick
morph: the tower topples; the bricks tumble and lock into the hooked magenta wrap 勹 along the top and right, while the buns squash into a heap that settles as the 巳 nested inside, completing 包
creativeAngle: 改走「疊高再倒塌」的實體笑料：花生的招牌動作（抱著太高的一疊東西、在錯誤時機敬禮）正是讓塔倒下的原因，倒塌本身把積木和包子摔成筆畫，取代前一版探長慢慢排字的做法；詞改用「包子」，畫面與字義、語音三者同一個故事。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean 3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 包 (bun / bag), correctly formed, in saturated solid magenta against a pale cream background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead: Peanut, a round-bellied cartoon raccoon sidekick in a tiny delivery cap, eager, clumsy, always saluting at the wrong moment. Supporting prop: a squad of chunky interlocking building bricks that march and stack themselves. Nothing busy behind: a flat cream floor and a faint shelf line.

0.0-1.5s: Peanut scurries in from the left hugging a tray of pale steamed buns already wobbling above his head. He spots the empty center of the floor, points, and plops the first bun down. The voice says the first 包 exactly as that bun lands with a soft squish.

1.5-3.5s: He stacks buns faster and faster, rising onto tiptoe, the tower swaying wider with every bun. The brick squad marches in from the right in a little line, climbs the tower, and stacks itself on top, which makes it sway even more. Peanut stretches to place one tiny last bun on the very top. Freeze: one still beat, tower leaning, his eyes wide.

3.5-4.5s: Proud of himself, Peanut lets go to snap a crisp salute. Wrong moment. The tower tips, bends, and comes down in a tumbling heap with a cartoon crash and a puff of flour. The bricks tumble and lock together into the hooked magenta wrap 勹, the short leading stroke at the top-left and the long hook curling across the top and down the right. The buns squash into a stacked heap that settles inside the hook as the 巳, its small closed top and the bottom bend sealed by a bun that rolls in last. The voice says the second 包 exactly as the glyph snaps solid and readable at 70% of frame height, with Peanut buried under a drift of spilled buns in the lower-left corner, only his eyes and cap poking out.

4.5-5.5s: The voice says 包子 as one fresh bun pops up out of the pile with a little puff of steam and plops onto Peanut's head. He blinks twice and grins.

5.5-8.0s: Final hold. The glyph 包 stays perfectly still, centered and clear. Away from the strokes, Peanut's paw pokes out of the bun pile and gives a wobbly salute, the bun on his head jiggles, and one leftover brick at the far right edge teeters and tips over with a tiny click.

Voice: one warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwan-standard Mandarin, slow with crisp tones, reads precisely 包、包、包子 (ㄅㄠ、ㄅㄠ、ㄅㄠ ˙ㄗ), character, character, word, and nothing after it. Any background music stays quieter than the voice. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 包 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects. No real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized cartoon animals, toys and bricks.
